name: Extreme Compression of Large Language Models via Additive Quantization
authors: Egiazarian, Muennighoff, Marafioti, Ruwase, Cheng, Marro, Ashkboos, Dehghani, Lueks
problem: 2-3 bit weight quantization of LLMs: existing methods degrade badly below 3 bits because uniform scalar grids cannot represent the weight distribution.
mechanism: Multi-Codebook Quantization (information-retrieval Additive Quantization) adapted to LLM weights: represent each weight vector as a SUM of selected codeword entries from several learned codebooks rather than a scalar on a uniform grid. Two innovations over classic AQ: the codebook assignment is INPUT-ADAPTIVE (a small network picks codewords per block of inputs rather than per weight in isolation), and codebook parameters are jointly optimized ACROSS transformer blocks instead of per-matrix. Ships fast GPU and CPU decode kernels.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claim (abstract): 'the first scheme that is Pareto optimal in terms of accuracy-vs-model-size when compressing to less than 3 bits per parameter', significantly improving on all known schemes in the 2-bit regime; and the fast implementations 'match or outperform optimized FP16 implementations for speed, while executing in a much smaller memory footprint'. COMPRESSION RATIO: up to ~8x at 2 bits/weight. QUALITY COST: the outperform-FP16-for-speed claim is the notable part - at 2-3 bits the decoder can be FASTER than FP16, not just smaller, because bandwidth drops faster than arithmetic rises.
